papers.title: Marigold V2: Revisiting Diffusion Transformers for Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.summary: Monocular depth estimation is a ubiquitous yet highly ill-posed computer vision task, with downstream applications in scene reconstruction, computational photography, and robotics, among others. Despite the field's maturity, recent models still struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution inputs and to produce sharp and detailed depth maps. papers.title: LRLS-v1.1: A Specification and Reference Simulation for Dual-Agent Exploration–Exploitation Under Hard Constraints
papers.summary: We present LRLS (Lobster RL Specification), a formal specification for constrained optimisation in which the classical exploration--exploitation trade-off is role-separated into two heterogeneous agent populations plus a scheduler. papers.title: A Dual-Evaluation Collaborative Decision Deep Reinforcement Learning Strategy for Multi-Constraint Energy Management of Hybrid Electric Vehicles
papers.summary: Coordinated control of fuel economy, state-of-charge (SOC), thermal state, and engine operation is central to hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) energy management. In existing discrete-action deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods, action selection usually relies on the Q-values predicted by the value network, whereas battery SOC and thermal constraints are often incorporated only through reward penalties after action execution. papers.title: Experimental Results and Reproducibility Package for Hierarchical Federated Reinforcement Learning in Electric Vehicle Charging
papers.summary: This deposit contains the simulation results for hierarchical federated deep reinforcement learning (HFDRL) applied to electric vehicle charging. It covers a 200-episode reward ablation study and a 1,000-episode policy comparison. The two archives include run-level results and analysis scripts. The accompanying reproducibility guide explains how to regenerate the reported results from the archived outputs and how to rerun the experiments.

papers.title: Topology-First B-Rep Meshing
papers.summary: Parametric boundary representation models (B-Reps) are the de facto standard in CAD, graphics, and robotics, yet converting them into valid meshes remains fragile. The difficulty originates from the unavoidable approximation of high-order surface and curve intersections to low-order primitives: the resulting geometric realization often fails to respect the exact topology encoded in the B-Rep, producing meshes with incorrect or missing adjacencies. papers.title: Handling techniques of an unbalanced stick tool in Goffin’s cockatoos (Cacatua goffiniana)
papers.summary: Abstract Parrots (Psittaciformes) exhibit unique morphological and behavioral traits that enable flexible, dexterous tool use, often comparable to that of apes. papers.title: DINOCT: robust skin surface localization for robotic noncontact dynamic optical coherence elastography
papers.summary: Noncontact dynamic optical coherence elastography (OCE) can measure the elastic properties of anterior soft tissues. However, applying OCE to skin requires tracking mechanical waves propagating in multiple directions to reconstruct mechanical anisotropy. Robotic scanning is well suited to this task but requires accurate probe positioning, alignment to the surface normal, and precise, repeatable rotation. papers.title: Derivation and Verification of Minimum Design Requirements for an Evaluation Treadmill Based on Humanoid Robot Specifications Analysis
papers.summary: As humanoid robot applications expand, there is a growing need for test environments that enable repeated and reproducible evaluation of walking performance. This study establishes minimum design requirements for an evaluation treadmill applicable to various humanoid robots. Public specifications of nine humanoid robots, including mass, payload, walking speed, and operating time, were analyzed to determine the required test load, belt speed, and operating time. papers.title: Multi-agent training for Pommerman: Curriculum learning and population-based self-play approach
papers.summary: Pommerman is a multi-agent environment that has received considerable attention from researchers in recent years. This environment is an ideal benchmark for multi-agent training, providing a battleground for two teams with communication capabilities among allied agents. Pommerman poses significant challenges for model-free reinforcement learning due to delayed action effects, sparse rewards, and false positives, where opponents can lose because of their own mistakes. papers.title: TD3-DLSAs: A Diffusion-Guided Low-Rank Transfer Reinforcement Learning Framework for 3D UAV Path Planning in Unknown Environments
papers.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) path planning in unknown 3D environments remains challenging due to missing prior maps, irregular terrain, and real-time obstacle avoidance requirements. This paper proposes TD3-DLSAs, a novel framework that integrates a conditional diffusion model with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) for transfer reinforcement learning. papers.summary: Part segmentation is a fundamental problem in computer graphics and 3D vision. papers.summary: This chapter provides an overview of the contemporary application of oral storytelling to people’s relations with ecology.
